title: The Church of the Nativity. The Alterations carried out by Justinian
author: E. T. Richmond
location_note: Church of the Nativity, Bethlehem; placed by name.
reading: p. 67 opening in full; then eligible-class keyword paragraphs (cistern passage pp. 70-71 in full)
notes: Justinianic atrium pier and column, floor levels, a semicircular retaining structure over the Grotto (1934 soundings), curved walling. The author asks whether the octagonal font was once a well-head over the cistern (question, not coded). The Grotto is the known cave, not a new feature.

features.site: north of the church axis, east of the semicircle (K)
features.subtype: large cistern reached by a square opening ringed by a plastered sloping channel with outflow and a stone circle
features.period: opening and channel cut through the earlier (pre-Justinianic) mosaic floor; cistern body not dated
features.quote: It gives access to a large cistern
